searched.title: Introduction to Bambu Nozzles | Bambu Lab Wiki
searched.note: Read in full from the cached HTML (the cached .txt omits the tab panels). The "Vortek Induction Nozzle" panel (purchase link "H2C Induction Hotend - Standard & High Flow") and the Nozzle-Printer Compatibility row "H2C Induction Hotend | H2C" are this product. It agrees with the store page on the sizes ("Size: 0.2mm/ 0.4mm/ 0.6mm/ 0.8mm"), the materials ("Materials: Hardened steel / Stainless steel") and the max temperature (350 ℃); the per-option diameter and material stay with the page's Size values (official_variant). It states no dimensions, weight, filament diameter, in-the-box list, flow rate or electrical value for this product. Its heating sentence ("Only about 8 seconds to reach printing temperature (e.g., 220°C) from room temperature") is an advantage claim with no registry key; not stored. "6 right hotends to be installed for alternating use" is printer capacity, not a spec of this product; not stored.

searched.title: Filament guide - Printer, Nozzle, AMS, Build Plate, Glue Compatibility and Required Parameters | Bambu Lab Wiki
searched.note: Linked from the store page ("Learn more about filament compatibility on Bambu Lab Wiki"). A general guide for every Bambu nozzle that does not name the H2C or the induction hotend, so none of its rows is stored as a spec of this product; it is used only to flag disagreements with this page's own Filament Compatibility table (the relations' conflict notes: PC and the TPUs at 0.2 mm, TPU 85A at 0.4 mm, PLA Aero at 0.2 mm). Where this page says "Not recommended" and the wiki "Not Compatible" (PETG Translucent at 0.2 mm), or this page is stricter than the wiki's "PLA*" row (PLA Silk family, PLA Galaxy, PLA Translucent, PLA Aero), no relation is recorded. Its nozzle temperature column is per filament, not a hotend limit.

searched.title: Introduction to the Workflow of the Vortek Induction Hotend | Bambu Lab Wiki
searched.note: Linked from the nozzles page panel for this product. It describes how the system works (induction heating assembly on the toolhead; on the hotend a U-shaped steel sleeve, an induction communication board, a hotend temperature NTC and an in-position detection magnet) and repeats the heating claim ("Only about 8 seconds to reach printing temperature (e.g., 220°C)"). It has no table and states no temperature limit, power, voltage, dimension or weight; nothing is stored from it.
